newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to Watch - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HEADLINE STOCKS -- Issues to Watch - Sept 5.

text.p: -- Kellogg Co said its third quarter earnings would fall short of the year-earlier $1.05 a share after a breakfast cereal price war.
Kellogg closed off 7/8 to 68-1/2 on Wednesday on the New York Stock Exchange. It slipped further, off 2-3/8 to 66-1/8, in after-hours trading.
-- McDonnell Douglas Corp is near a $1.3 billion deal to sell up to 12 cargo jets to Lufthansa AG, the Wall Street Journal reported. McDonnell Douglas closed at 49-7/8.
-- Boeing Co is in talks about wing parts with Japanese manufacturers, the Wall Street Journal reported. Boeing closed off 3/4 to 91-3/8.
-- Campbell Soup posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.73 a share, up from $0.57 a year earlier, after the market close on Wednesday. Campbell finished at 67-1/2.
-- IBM plans to announce a "network" computer, to replace personal computers in corporate settings, according to the Wall Street Journal. IBM closed at 114-3/4.
-- Oxford Health said it expects 1997 earnings growth near 50 percent. The health maintenance organization closed up 1-3/8 to 45-1/8.
